numbering_convention: Full-length precursor numbering, including the N-terminal signal peptide. This is the numbering used in PDB 6QGC/5XG0 and consistently throughout the FAST-PETase, ThermoPETase, and HotPETase literature (e.g. S121E, D186H, R280A).

catalytic_triad.role: Canonical Ser-His-Asp hydrolase triad. Ser160 is the covalent nucleophile that attacks the scissile ester bond; His237 deprotonates Ser160 and later the leaving group; Asp206 orients/stabilizes His237.
catalytic_triad.notes: Mutating any of these three positions is expected to abolish or severely impair catalytic activity in almost all cases. Flag automatically regardless of ESM-2 score.
catalytic_triad.source: Han et al. 2017, Nat Commun 8:2106; Joo et al. 2018, Nat Commun 9:382

oxyanion_hole.role: Backbone NH groups stabilize the negatively charged oxyanion of the tetrahedral reaction intermediate.
oxyanion_hole.notes: Sits immediately adjacent to the nucleophile (Met161 is Ser160+1). Side-chain identity matters less than backbone geometry, but large substitutions can still disrupt hole geometry.

substrate_binding_notable_residues.role: Trp159 and Trp185 form aromatic stacking interactions with the PET aromatic rings across subsites I/II of the binding cleft; Arg280 anchors substrate at the far end of subsite IIc.
substrate_binding_notable_residues.notes: These are prime substrate-binding-affinity engineering targets rather than purely disruptive positions. Note that R280A is itself part of ThermoPETase/FAST-PETase, so mutation here is not automatically bad -- it needs case-by-case interpretation, unlike the catalytic triad.
substrate_binding_notable_residues.source: Joo et al. 2018, Nat Commun 9:382; Austin et al. 2018, PNAS
